Subject: Request: consolidated VM artifacts for SIG/CAIQ review

Hi Naomi —

Thanks for working with us on the SIG/CAIQ validation. Brightline needs a concise bundle that maps your vulnerability management outputs to the SIG controls (Vuln discovery cadence, triage SLAs, CVE closure evidence).

Can you:
- Share a single CSV mapping scan cadence -> control IDs -> evidence filenames
- Confirm any SLA exceptions (e.g., 30/60/90-day windows) and which CVEs they apply to
- Provide a short attestation we can include in our report (one paragraph)

Deadline for the package: Friday, 2029-06-21 EOD (auditor ingestion window).

If you expect any exceptions beyond normal SLA (we've seen legacy deps require 30 days), flag them now so we can annotate the report.

Appreciate it —
Elena Ramos
Security Assurance Lead, FinEdge Payments
elena.ramos@finedge.com

Elena —

Thanks for the clear ask and the deadline. We're preparing a consolidated proof map that maps our weekly scan cadence, triage SLA, and closure artifacts back to the SIG/CAIQ control IDs.

I've attached a working CSV (vm-proof-map.csv) and a calendar export for our next three scan windows (scan-schedule.ics).

Quick notes:
- Standard SLA: critical CVEs (CVSS >= 9) = 7 days to patch/mitigate; high (7-8.9) = 30 days; medium = 90 days for non-prod-impacting items.
- We have one requested exception for a legacy third-party library (see referenced CVEs below) where the fix requires vendor coordination; proposed SLA = 30 days for closure tracking and documented compensating controls while patching is scheduled.

Elena, please confirm if an annotated exception (with justification and a 30-day remediation plan) is acceptable for your intake. If yes, we'll include a signed one-paragraph attestation and a short CVE closure log.

Looping in Kimberly and Marissa to finalize the closure log and exception wording.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference
